items.text: Reduction to S' affine

$S'$ quasi-compact: replace it by the disjoint sum $\bar S'$ of finitely many affine opens (faithfully flat, quasi-compact, affine). If $\bar S'\to S$ factors through $S'\to S$ and is of 1- (2-)descent, so is $S'\to S$.
A morphism that has a section is of effective descent (the identity is).
The case with a section
Section $\sigma$: $\sigma^*\circ g^*\simeq\mathrm{id}$, so $F_S\to F_{S'}$ is faithful. Fully faithful: from $u'\colon M'\to N'$ compatible with gluing data take $\sigma^*u'\colon M\to N$.
Effectivity: for $M'$ with descent data put $M=\sigma^*M'$; the descent datum gives $g^*M\simeq M'$. Only a cosimplicial category is used.
General principle
$\bar S\to S$ of 2-descent, and the base change $\bar S'\to\bar S$ has a section (i.e. there is an $S$-morphism $\bar S\to S'$). Then $S'\to S$ is of 2-descent.
$M'$ over $S'$ with descent data w.r.t. $S$: $\bar M'$ has descent data w.r.t. $\bar S$, so comes from a unique $\bar M$ on $\bar S$.

On $\bar{\bar S}=\bar S\times_S\bar S$ the two inverse images of $\bar M$ are isomorphic (by 1-descent for the base change with a section); this is a gluing datum, a descent datum (diagram chase), so $\bar M$ descends to $M$ on $S$.
The affine case
$A\to A'$ faithfully flat, $M'$ an $A'$-module with descent data $M'\otimes_AA'\simeq A'\otimes_AM'$ (cocycle on the triple tensor product):
M=\ker\bigl(M'\rightrightarrows M''\bigr),\qquad M\otimes_AA'\longrightarrow M'\ \text{compatible with descent data}
This is an isomorphism after the faithfully flat extension $A\to A'$ (where there is a section), hence an isomorphism: $M'$ descends.
Descent of subsheaves
$\mathcal F$ quasi-coherent on $S$, $\mathcal F'$, $\mathcal F''$ its inverse images; $g$ faithfully flat quasi-compact:
\{\text{q.c. subsheaves of }\mathcal F\}\longrightarrow\{\text{q.c. subsheaves of }\mathcal F'\}\rightrightarrows\{\text{q.c. subsheaves of }\mathcal F''\}\qquad\text{exact}

A subsheaf $\mathcal G'\subset\mathcal F'$ with $p_1^*\mathcal G'=p_2^*\mathcal G'$ is stable under the descent data, hence comes from $\mathcal G$; and $\mathcal G\to\mathcal F$ is injective after base change, hence injective.
Descent of subschemes

Same exactness for subsets $P(S)\to P(S')\rightrightarrows P(S'')$ ($g$ surjective), for open subsets ($S$ has the quotient topology), for closed subsets, for closed subschemes (= q.c. ideals) and for open subschemes.
\{\text{subschemes }Z\subset S\ \text{retrocompact}\}\longrightarrow\{Z'\subset S'\}\rightrightarrows\{Z''\subset S''\}\qquad\text{exact (retrocompact }Z')
Injectivity: $T\mapsto g^{-1}T$ on subobjects ($T_1\cap T_2\to T_i$ isomorphic after base change, hence isomorphic).
Subobject (monomorphism) is more general than subscheme: the point plus the complement of the point in the line; the normalization of a node minus one point.
Exactness: $Z'$ has two equal inverse images in $S''$, so $Z'=g^{-1}(Z)$ as sets; $Z$ is locally closed:
Z=g(Z'),\ Z'\to S\ \text{quasi-compact}\Rightarrow g^{-1}\bar Z=\overline{Z'},\qquad Z\ \text{open in }\bar Z\ (\text{quotient topology})
Then $Z$ is closed in an open $U$, $Z'$ closed in $U'$: closed subschemes descend.
Descent of morphisms of schemes
Theorem. $g\colon S'\to S$ faithfully flat and quasi-compact is of 1-descent for relative schemes: for $X,Y$ over $S$,
\operatorname{Hom}_S(X,Y)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Hom}_{S'}(X',Y')\rightrightarrows\operatorname{Hom}_{S''}(X'',Y'')\qquad\text{exact}
Proof: a morphism $X\to Y$ is a subscheme $Z$ of $X\times_SY$ whose first projection to $X$ is an isomorphism (the graph).
